# Skill map

Every skill the router may name, grouped by practice area. The description
is the skill's own trigger text: what it does, when to use it and when not to.

## Getting Started (`getting-started`)

- **`setup`** — Set up Legal Skills for a practice. Asks role, jurisdictions and practice areas, drafts the profiles those areas need from the starter profiles, and saves them where you choose. Run by typing it; never approves a profile.
- **`start`** — Start work on a matter. Plans which Legal Skills to run in order with the human decision at each step, then runs one step at a time with your go-ahead. Run by typing it with the facts; never answers the legal question itself.
- **`check-citations`** — Check every case citation, legislation reference and quoted passage in a draft against the official publishers and return one status table. Run by typing it with the draft; never marks a reference verified itself.
- **`help`** — Show what Legal Skills covers, the practice areas, what to type for common tasks and which profiles this session has. Run by typing it; gives no legal advice.

## Australian AI Governance (`ai-governance`)

- **`assess-board-ai-oversight`** — Issue-spot board and director-duty exposure from AI adoption and board use of AI under the Corporations Act. Use for board AI policies, AI-assisted board packs and oversight reviews. Never concludes breach or compliance.
- **`check-ai-guidance-alignment`** — Assess AI governance documents against Australian voluntary guidance, including Guidance for AI Adoption, the Voluntary AI Safety Standard and ISO/IEC 42001. Use for gap assessments and AI policy reviews. Never certifies or concludes compliance.
- **`configure-ai-governance-profile`** — Create or update the AI-governance profile the Australian AI-governance skills run against, recording entity type, sector, overlays and governing documents. Use for first setup or changes. Never approves the profile.
- **`map-ai-regulatory-obligations`** — Map which Australian regulatory instruments bind a described AI use case and flag pending ones as watch items. Use for AI adoption, procurement and product launches. Not for privacy depth or the EU AI Act.
- **`track-ai-regulatory-developments`** — Check the Australian AI regulatory watch list on demand against primary sources and report what changed. Use for horizon reviews or before advice that depends on a pending instrument. Never treats a pending instrument as law.
- **`triage-government-ai-use-case`** — Route an Australian government AI use case to its assurance track, either the Commonwealth DTA policy or a state or territory framework. Use for government AI adoption and procurement. Not for private-sector obligations.

## Australian AML/CTF (`aml-ctf`)

- **`configure-aml-ctf-practice-profile`** — Create or update the AML/CTF practice profile for an Australian legal practice under the tranche 2 reforms. Use before any other AML/CTF workflow. Never decides whether a service is designated or approves the profile.
- **`map-designated-services`** — Map whether an Australian legal practice's services are designated services under the AML/CTF Act tranche 2 reforms. Use when a service line may trigger AML/CTF obligations. Not for other sectors. Never decides enrolment.
- **`map-reporting-obligations`** — Map which AML/CTF reports an Australian legal practice may need for a scenario, including suspicious matter reports, tipping-off and legal professional privilege. Never decides a matter is suspicious or drafts a report.
- **`review-aml-ctf-program`** — Issue-spot an Australian legal practice's AML/CTF program, risk assessment, policies, governance and customer due diligence design. Use for gap reviews of draft or approved programs. Never certifies compliance.
- **`track-aml-ctf-developments`** — Check the AML/CTF watch register for developments affecting Australian legal practices and report what changed, what is pending and what now binds. Never treats a pending instrument as in force.

## Australian Commercial Drafting (`commercial-drafting`)

- **`configure-drafting-profile`** — Create or update the profile for first-draft Australian commercial documents, recording the drafting party, governing state, house style and standard positions. Use before commercial drafting. Never approves the profile.
- **`draft-nda`** — Prepare a first-draft mutual or one-way Australian NDA from party details and commercial instructions for lawyer review. Not for restraints, guaranteeing secrecy or approving execution.
- **`draft-privacy-policy`** — Draft an Australian private-sector privacy policy from evidenced data practices, with an APP 1.4 map and overseas disclosure and marketing controls. Never invents data practices or publishes the policy.
- **`draft-services-agreement`** — Prepare a first-draft Australian B2B services or contractor agreement and statement of work for lawyer review. Flags worker classification for employment review. Never approves execution.
- **`draft-website-terms`** — Prepare first-draft Australian SaaS or subscription website terms for consumers and small businesses, preserving consumer guarantees and flagging unfair terms. Not for financial products or publication.
- **`review-draft-against-checklist`** — Review an Australian commercial draft for missing clauses, undefined terms, broken references, placeholders and unfair-contract-terms risk. Returns a prioritised issues table. Never certifies enforceability.

## Australian Consumer & Competition (`consumer-competition`)

- **`assess-cartel-and-rpm-risk`** — Issue-spot Australian cartel, concerted practice, resale price maintenance, exclusive dealing and market-power risk. Use for competitor contacts, distribution restraints and pricing pressure. Never concludes an offence occurred.
- **`assess-consumer-guarantees`** — Assess Australian Consumer Law guarantee issues, remedies, manufacturer exposure and warranty documents for lawyer review. Use for defects, failed services and refund disputes. Never decides entitlement.
- **`configure-consumer-competition-profile`** — Create or validate the business profile the Australian consumer and competition skills run against. Use before assessment for scope, evidence owners and approval controls. Never approves the profile.
- **`map-merger-notification`** — Map Australian mandatory merger notification thresholds, exemptions, waivers and stay pathways from transaction evidence. Use before signing or completion planning. Never lodges an application or approves closing.
- **`map-product-safety-obligations`** — Map Australian product safety standards, bans, recalls and mandatory incident reporting from product and event evidence. Use for supply checks, injury reports and recall planning. Never executes a recall or files a report.
- **`review-marketing-claims`** — Review Australian marketing, environmental, comparative and pricing claims across the purchase journey, including drip pricing. Use before a campaign. Never certifies claims or publishes advertisements.
- **`track-accc-developments`** — Check the ACCC watch register on demand against official sources for changed merger, consumer, competition and product safety positions. Use before advice or a horizon review. Not an unattended monitor.

## Australian Contract Review (`contract-review`)

- **`build-negotiation-redline-memo`** — Draft an Australian contract negotiation memo with current text, proposed text, rationale and authorised fallbacks per clause. Use after a contract review. Never sends the memo or alters a live document.
- **`check-unfair-contract-terms`** — Screen Australian contract terms for unfair-contract-terms risk under the ACL or ASIC Act. Use for consumer or small-business standard-form contracts. Never declares a term invalid.
- **`configure-review-playbook`** — Create or update an Australian contract-review playbook of standard positions, fallbacks and approval thresholds by clause type. Use before inbound contract review. Never invents firm positions or approves the playbook.
- **`review-commercial-agreement`** — Review a supplied Australian MSA, SaaS, supply or services agreement against approved positions and return a clause-referenced issues table. Never silently rewrites or approves execution.
- **`review-limitation-and-indemnity-regime`** — Review interacting caps, exclusions, indemnities, insurance and proportionate liability in an Australian commercial contract. Use for risk-allocation review. Never assumes contracting out is permitted.
- **`track-contract-renewals`** — Build or review a source-linked register of Australian contract renewal and notice dates and auto-renewal risks. Use for a contract portfolio or an impending renewal. Never sends notices or updates live diaries.
- **`triage-inbound-nda`** — Triage a supplied inbound Australian NDA as green, yellow or red against a review playbook, with clause references and escalation. Never clears execution or certifies enforceability.

## Australian Corporations Governance (`corporations-governance`)

- **`assess-director-duties-governance`** — Issue-spot Australian director and officer duty risks for a proposed or completed company decision. Use for authority, care, reliance, conflicts and solvency checks. Never concludes breach, validity or solvency.
- **`configure-corporations-governance`** — Create or update the governance profile for an Australian company, recording entity type, governing documents, board authority and delegations. Use before other corporations-governance skills. Never approves the profile.
- **`maintain-corporations-governance-calendar`** — Create or update a source-linked governance calendar for an Australian company, covering meetings, records, notifications and reporting checkpoints. Never submits filings or sends notices. Not for tax or employment calendars.
- **`prepare-board-decision-record`** — Prepare draft Australian company board materials, including a board paper, resolution or minutes extract, from verified law and supplied evidence. Never invents attendance, votes or reasons, and never circulates documents.
- **`review-corporations-governance-framework`** — Review an Australian company's governance framework against Corporations Act requirements and produce a gap and action matrix. Use for board authority, delegations, conflicts and records. Never certifies compliance.

## Australian Employment & Fair Work (`employment-fair-work`)

- **`assess-discrimination-and-positive-duty`** — Map Australian workplace discrimination and positive-duty exposure under Commonwealth, NSW, Victorian and Queensland law. Use for incident or preventive-control reviews. Never determines liability or certifies compliance.
- **`assess-employee-vs-contractor`** — Issue-spot Australian employee or contractor classification and sham contracting under the Fair Work Act. Use before contractor drafting or an engagement review. Never classifies conclusively from an ABN or label.
- **`assess-restraint-of-trade`** — Issue-spot Australian employment restraints against common-law reasonableness, NSW legislation and proposed non-compete reforms. Use for exit or clause reviews. Never certifies enforceability.
- **`assess-termination-exposure`** — Issue-spot exposure from an Australian dismissal or redundancy, covering unfair dismissal, general protections, redundancy and notice. Use before a dismissal decision or when a claim is threatened. Never concludes a dismissal was unfair.
- **`compute-underpayment-exposure-framework`** — Prepare an Australian underpayment exposure framework from entitlement sources, payroll evidence and limitation leads. Use for wage underpayment reviews. Never invents award rates or computes a final liability.
- **`configure-employment-profile`** — Create or update the employer profile the Fair Work skills run against, recording coverage basis, size, awards, agreements and policies. Use before other employment workflows. Never decides coverage or approves the profile.
- **`map-fair-work-obligations`** — Map which Fair Work Act, National Employment Standards, award and enterprise agreement provisions apply to an Australian employment arrangement. Use for onboarding, contract design and entitlement queries. Never concludes award coverage or calculates pay.
- **`review-employment-contract`** — Review an Australian employment contract against the NES, award coverage, set-off, IP, confidentiality, termination and fixed-term limits. Use for onboarding or contract refreshes. Never certifies compliance.
- **`review-workplace-policy`** — Review an Australian employer's workplace policies against Fair Work Act hooks such as right to disconnect, flexible work, leave and delegates' rights. Use for policy refreshes. Never certifies compliance or drafts policy text.
- **`track-fair-work-developments`** — Check the Fair Work watch register on demand against primary sources, including amending Acts, the Annual Wage Review and indexed thresholds. Use for horizon reviews. Never treats a pending instrument as law.

## Australian Estate Planning (`estate-planning`)

- **`assemble-nsw-estate-documents`** — Draft a NSW will, enduring power of attorney and enduring guardianship from a firm's approved precedents for solicitor review. Not for other jurisdictions, trusts, probate or self-represented people.
- **`assemble-qld-estate-documents`** — Draft a Queensland will and enduring power of attorney from a firm's approved precedents for solicitor review. Not for other jurisdictions, advance health directives, trusts or probate.
- **`assemble-vic-estate-documents`** — Draft a Victorian will, enduring power of attorney and medical treatment decision maker appointment from a firm's approved precedents for solicitor review. Not for other jurisdictions, trusts or probate.

## Australian Legal Research (`legal-research`)

- **`check-act-legislation`** — Verify ACT legislation at the official ACT legislation register, covering whether it is in force, the version on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for other jurisdictions, Bills, case law or interpretation.
- **`check-commonwealth-legislation`** — Verify Commonwealth Acts and instruments on the Federal Register of Legislation, covering whether in force, the compilation on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for State or Territory law, Bills or case law.
- **`check-court-ai-protocol`** — Check which Australian court or tribunal generative AI practice note applies to a document being filed, what it bans and what disclosure it needs. Use before filing affidavits, witness statements, expert reports or submissions prepared with AI help.
- **`check-northern-territory-legislation`** — Verify Northern Territory legislation at the official NT legislation database, covering whether it is in force, the version on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for other jurisdictions, Bills, case law or interpretation.
- **`check-nsw-legislation`** — Verify NSW Acts, statutory instruments and planning instruments on the official NSW legislation website, covering whether in force, the version on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for other jurisdictions, Bills, court rules or case law.
- **`check-queensland-legislation`** — Verify Queensland legislation at the official Queensland legislation publisher, covering whether it is in force, the version on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for other jurisdictions, Bills, case law or interpretation.
- **`check-south-australia-legislation`** — Verify South Australian legislation at the official SA legislation publisher, covering whether it is in force, the version on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for other jurisdictions, Bills, case law or interpretation.
- **`check-tasmania-legislation`** — Verify Tasmanian legislation at the official Tasmanian legislation publisher, covering whether it is in force, the version on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for other jurisdictions, Bills, case law or interpretation.
- **`check-victoria-legislation`** — Verify Victorian Acts and statutory rules at the official Victorian legislation publisher, covering whether in force, the version on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for other jurisdictions, Bills, case law or interpretation.
- **`check-western-australia-legislation`** — Verify Western Australian legislation at the official WA legislation publisher, covering whether it is in force, the version on a date and whether a citation matches. Not for other jurisdictions, Bills, case law or interpretation.
- **`format-aglc4-citations`** — Draft, convert, review and correct Australian legal citations and bibliographies in AGLC4 format. Use for footnotes, pinpoints, subsequent references and citation audits. Does not verify that a cited source exists.
- **`route-case-citation`** — Use first to verify or check any Australian case citation, judgment or authority, including documents with possibly fabricated citations. Identifies the court and routes to the right verifier. Not for case treatment or foreign citations.
- **`trace-commonwealth-legislative-change`** — Trace what changed in a Commonwealth provision between two dates, which amendment made the change and when it commenced, from Federal Register versions. Not for Bills, State law or interpretation.
- **`verify-case-quote`** — Verify that a quoted passage attributed to an Australian judgment appears in the decision at the official court publisher, with its paragraph location. Use after the citation is verified. Not for paraphrase or interpretation.
- **`verify-federal-judgment`** — Verify that a Federal Court or Federal Circuit and Family Court decision exists at the official publisher, for FCA, FCAFC, FedCFamC, FCCA, FamCA and FCR citations. Use via route-case-citation. Not for case treatment.
- **`verify-hca-judgment`** — Verify that a High Court of Australia decision exists at the official High Court website, for HCA, CLR and ALJR citations. Use via route-case-citation or for a known High Court citation. Not for case treatment.
- **`verify-nsw-judgment`** — Verify that a NSW court or tribunal decision exists on NSW Caselaw, for medium-neutral NSW citations and NSWLR. Use via route-case-citation or for a known NSW citation. Not for case treatment.
- **`verify-qld-judgment`** — Verify that a Queensland court or tribunal decision exists at the Queensland Judgments website, for medium-neutral Queensland citations and Qd R. Use via route-case-citation or for a known Queensland citation. Not for case treatment.

## Australian Litigation Deadlines (`litigation-deadlines`)

- **`compute-procedural-deadlines`** — Compute candidate Australian civil court deadlines from a lawyer-supplied trigger date, never by model arithmetic. Use for defences, appeals and other rule-fixed steps. Not for criminal procedure or contested trigger dates.
- **`configure-litigation-deadline-profile`** — Create or update the practice profile the litigation-deadlines skills require, recording forums, the named confirmer and the diary system. Use before first use. Never computes a date or approves the profile.
- **`maintain-deadline-register`** — Build and update a source-linked deadline register for one Australian civil litigation matter, with each entry's rule, trigger and confirmation status. Not the practice's diary. Never confirms a date.
- **`map-limitation-periods`** — Map an Australian civil cause of action to candidate limitation periods across state, territory and Commonwealth law, flagging extensions and special regimes. Never determines accrual or picks a binding date. Not for criminal matters.
- **`map-tribunal-review-deadlines`** — Map and compute candidate merits-review and tribunal deadlines for Australian decisions, never by model arithmetic, covering the ART, NCAT, QCAT and VCAT. Use after a government or tribunal decision. Never concludes a period has expired.
- **`verify-deadline-basis`** — Verify the court-rule and public-holiday tables behind the litigation-deadlines skills against official publishers. Use before first computed reliance or when a rule change is suspected. Never computes dates.

## Australian Privacy & Cybersecurity (`privacy-cybersecurity`)

- **`assess-ai-privacy-cybersecurity-use-case`** — Assess an AI use case for Australian privacy and cybersecurity suitability, covering data flows, harms, vendors and controls. Use for AI intake, procurement, pilots and privacy impact assessments. Not for AI obligations mapping or board oversight.
- **`assess-australian-data-breach`** — Triage a suspected Australian data breach or cyber incident for lawyers, mapping breach regimes, reporting clocks and an action matrix. Use for unauthorised access, ransomware and vendor incidents. Never decides whether to notify.
- **`assess-australian-privacy-issues`** — Spot and structure Australian privacy and data protection issues from facts, contracts, policies or data maps into a source-linked issue matrix. Use for privacy scoping and applicability. Not for case law or final opinions.
- **`assess-automated-decision-transparency`** — Assess Australian privacy transparency duties for automated and AI-assisted decisions, including APP 1.7 to 1.9 from 10 December 2026 and WA PRIS. Use for decision inventories and privacy policy readiness. Not for discrimination law.
- **`assess-statutory-privacy-tort`** — Screen facts against the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). Use for surveillance, recording, scraping, deepfakes and disclosure of intimate, health or location information. Legislation only, no case law.
- **`check-australian-privacy-principles`** — Verify the Australian Privacy Principles, coverage, exemptions, codes and pending amendments from official sources. Use whenever a workflow relies on an APP or reuses an earlier APP analysis. No case law.
- **`map-australian-cyber-incident-obligations`** — Map concurrent Australian cyber incident, data breach, ransomware payment, critical infrastructure and sector reporting duties by entity, trigger, recipient and clock. For full incident triage use assess-australian-data-breach.
- **`route-australian-privacy-jurisdiction`** — Route Australian privacy, health information, data breach, surveillance and workplace monitoring issues to the Commonwealth, State and Territory regimes that may apply. Use before substantive privacy or breach analysis.

## Australian Work Health & Safety (`work-health-safety`)

- **`assess-notifiable-incident`** — Urgent preliminary assessment of an Australian workplace incident, covering candidate notifiable incident, who notifies which regulator, how fast, and site preservation. Use straight after an incident. Never decides whether to notify.
- **`assess-officer-due-diligence`** — Review evidence that an Australian company's officers exercise WHS due diligence, element by element, with gaps and board questions. Use for board WHS reviews and post-incident governance. Never concludes due diligence was met.
- **`map-whs-duties`** — Map who holds which work health and safety duties for an Australian business, worksite or contractor arrangement under the model WHS Act or Victoria's OHS Act. Use for onboarding and multi-party sites. Never concludes a breach.
- **`review-psychosocial-risk-controls`** — Gap-check an Australian employer's psychosocial risk management against the governing WHS regulations and code of practice. Use for risk-register reviews and regulator information requests. Never certifies compliance or investigates a complaint.
- **`track-whs-developments`** — Check the Australian work health and safety watch register on demand, including each jurisdiction's adoption of model WHS law changes. Use for horizon reviews. Never treats a Bill or draft code as law in force.

## Legal Evidence Workflows (`evidence-workflows`)

- **`build-document-index`** — Build a numbered, source-linked document index as a Word file from supplied matter documents, usable as a court-book or bundle index. Use for litigation, investigations and disclosure. Never decides relevance, privilege or admissibility.
- **`build-evidence-chronology`** — Build a source-linked evidence chronology as a Word file from supplied matter documents, keeping exact date wording, conflicts and gaps. Use for litigation, investigations and disputes. Never decides credibility, weight or merits.
- **`build-privilege-log`** — Draft a privilege log as a Word file from supplied matter documents, one row per document with the claimed basis and waiver flags. Use for discovery, subpoenas and regulatory productions. Never decides that privilege exists or is lost.
- **`map-evidence-inconsistencies`** — Map where supplied matter documents and accounts agree, diverge or are silent on each material fact, as a Word file. Use after a chronology, for witness preparation and cross-examination planning. Never decides which account is right.

## Legal Triage (`triage`)

- **`configure-legal-triage`** — Create or update a community legal centre's enquiry triage profile, recording service scope, urgency pathways, eligibility and referrals. Use before legal triage. Never invents centre policy or approves the profile.
- **`triage-legal-enquiry`** — Prepare a provisional triage record for a legal enquiry at an Australian community legal centre under its approved profile, covering urgency, issue and referral. For authorised staff only. Not a public chatbot and never gives legal advice.

## Legal Cognitive Sparring (`cognitive-sparring`)

- **`clarify-burden-and-standard`** — For a lawyer's own case: who bears the burden, to what standard, and what evidence meets it on their facts. For hidden premises use `$map-assumptions`. Never invents a standard or decides it is met.
- **`drill-oral-advocacy`** — Hostile bench questions or an opening or closing drill, scored on clarity, concessions and recovery. For a written case use `$role-play-decision-maker`. Never predicts a ruling.
- **`find-blind-spots`** — Gaps in a lawyer's analysis: unaddressed questions, facts, parties, procedures, authorities, as must-check or nice-to-have. For premises use `$map-assumptions`. Never invents authority.
- **`map-assumptions`** — Use when a lawyer wants the stated and hidden assumptions behind a view surfaced, ranked and tested. For unaddressed issues use `$find-blind-spots`. Never fills a gap from memory.
- **`oppose-as-counsel`** — Argue the other side with the strongest counters a lawyer must answer, speculation labelled. For a judge's view use `$role-play-decision-maker`. Never advises the other side or invents a citation.
- **`pressure-test-argument`** — Sparring for a lawyer's own argument: stress-test it for weak premises, leaps, missing authorities and adverse facts. For the other side use `$oppose-as-counsel`. Never gives final advice or invents a citation.
- **`pressure-test-strategy`** — Challenge a lawyer's forum, timing, settlement and escalation choices for unstated risks. For arguments use `$pressure-test-argument`. Never files or contacts a counterparty.
- **`red-team-evidence`** — Challenge the evidence behind a lawyer's position on provenance, hearsay, weight and gaps. For the argument itself use `$pressure-test-argument`. Never decides admissibility or invents a source.
- **`role-play-decision-maker`** — Use when a lawyer wants a named judge, tribunal member or regulator played: what would persuade or fail. For rehearsal use `$drill-oral-advocacy`. Never predicts an outcome as certain.
- **`simplify-without-losing-precision`** — Plain-language restatement of a position a client could follow, then flags what simplifying hid, for a lawyer. To quiz the lawyer use `$test-understanding`. Never sends it to the client.
- **`steelman-then-attack`** — Restate a lawyer's position in its strongest form, then attack it in a separate phase. For a one-step critique use `$pressure-test-argument`. Never merges the phases or invents authority.
- **`test-understanding`** — Quiz a lawyer on a named concept or matter: short questions, sources demanded, gaps marked. For their argument use `$pressure-test-argument`. Never lectures or invents an authority.
